question:
A surveyor records the vertices of a quadrilateral as $A(0,0)$, $B(6,0)$, $C(8,4)$, and $D(2,6)$, taken in order. To check the area calculation, the surveyor first divides the quadrilateral along diagonal $AC$ and later repeats the calculation using diagonal $BD$. The determinant formula for the area of a triangle is used in both divisions so that the two independently obtained totals can be compared.

(a) Calculate the area of $\triangle ABC$.

(b) Calculate the area of $\triangle ACD$.

(c) Hence, determine the area of quadrilateral $ABCD$.

(d) Verify the result by finding the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle BCD$.
explanation:
(a)
Using the determinant formula,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ABC=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 & 1\\6 & 0 & 1\\8 & 4 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|0-0+(24-0)|=12$$
Therefore, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $12$ square units.

(b)
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ACD=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 & 1\\8 & 4 & 1\\2 & 6 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|0-0+(48-8)|=20$$
Therefore, the area of $\triangle ACD$ is $20$ square units.

(c)
Diagonal $AC$ divides the quadrilateral into $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ACD$. Hence,
$$\text{Area of }ABCD=12+20=32$$
Thus, the area of the quadrilateral is $32$ square units.

(d)
Using diagonal $BD$,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle ABD=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 & 1\\6 & 0 & 1\\2 & 6 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|=\frac{1}{2}(36)=18$$
Also,
$$\text{Area of }\triangle BCD=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}6 & 0 & 1\\8 & 4 & 1\\2 & 6 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|6(4-6)+(48-8)|$$
$$=\frac{1}{2}|-12+40|=14$$
Therefore,
$$\text{Area of }ABCD=18+14=32$$
The area obtained using diagonal $BD$ agrees with the earlier result.

options.A:
(a) $12$ square units
(b) $20$ square units
(c) $32$ square units
(d) $[\triangle ABD]=18$ and $[\triangle BCD]=14$ square units, giving $32$ square units
options.B:
(a) $12$ square units
(b) $16$ square units
(c) $28$ square units
(d) $[\triangle ABD]=18$ and $[\triangle BCD]=10$ square units, giving $28$ square units

(c) $44$ square units
